headline: High: Aci’s broad egress plus MemMachine’s MCP/API surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server, and MemMachine exposes an MCP Server; that shared bridge makes instruction-like content in one agent’s outputs plausibly reachable by the other. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so I cannot rule out prompt injection. This is more than manual copy-paste, but not clearly high because no raw web-content parser is documented.
conditions: IF Aci forwards MemMachine output into tool prompts without provenance tagging
IF both agents are connected through the same MCP server or message bridge
IF either agent treats retrieved text as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic tool-chaining between the agents
Add provenance labels to all cross-agent messages
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for the bridge
Insert a human review step before executing instructions from the other agent
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can be reached via MCP/API. If Aci passes sensitive records into MemMachine, MemMachine’s context can be exposed through its networked interfaces. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without special setup.
conditions: IF Aci sends CRM/email/calendar content into MemMachine context
IF MemMachine logs or re-emits stored conversational context through its API
IF both agents are used on the same sensitive workspace
mitigations: Limit cross-agent payloads to redacted summaries
Block sensitive fields from being forwarded to MemMachine
Turn off or minimize retention for shared conversations
Review outbound destinations for Aci before enabling the pair
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on the bridge

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci supports multiple instances and has broad network egress; MemMachine exposes REST, SDK, and MCP interfaces. The profiles do not show shared filesystem writes, but they do show overlapping mutable networked surfaces that can conflict if both act on the same external resources or shared MCP endpoint. Uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external CRM or API resource
IF both are pointed at the same MCP server without locking
IF Aci runs multiple instances against the same account
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or API keys
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use per-agent namespaces in shared services
Add optimistic-lock retries on mutable records
requires-engineering: implement distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and MemMachine is designed for conversational memory via API/MCP. If Aci’s outputs are fed into MemMachine and then reused as authoritative context, errors can propagate into downstream actions or recommendations. The profiles show no verification gate, so the pair is dangerous by default when chained.
conditions: IF MemMachine treats Aci output as authoritative memory
IF downstream workflows act on MemMachine context without verification
IF Aci-generated facts are reused in later customer-facing actions
mitigations: Require source citations on all imported facts
Add a verification step before memory writes
Keep Aci outputs out of persistent memory by default
Review high-impact actions before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and audit trails

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, support, and calendar data, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a mismatch in how those data classes are stored or retained is plausible. I cannot prove a specific violation, but the uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Aci data is retained longer in MemMachine than in the source system
IF EU or regulated personal data is forwarded into MemMachine storage
IF the deployment requires deletion/export guarantees across both agents
mitigations: Map each data class to a retention policy
Exclude regulated fields from MemMachine storage
Document residency for every downstream API
Test deletion/export on a sample record
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
